mil5.1.5:0.4: 5. Question Concerning King Sivi’s Gift of His Eyes
mil5.1.5:1.2: ‘King Sivi gave his eyes to a beggar, and though he was blind, divine eyes arose in him again.’ This statement is contradictory, refutable, and flawed. It is said in the suttas: ‘When the cause is destroyed, there is no arising of the divine eye in what is without cause and without basis.’ If, Venerable Nāgasena, King Sivi gave his eyes to a beggar, then the statement ‘divine eyes arose again’ is false.
mil5.1.5:1.3: If divine eyes arose, then the statement ‘King Sivi gave his eyes to a beggar’ is also false.
mil5.1.5:1.4: This question has two horns; it is more knotted than knotted, more entangled than entangled, more difficult than difficult. It has come to you—explain your view on this matter for the refutation of the opposing doctrines.”
